title: SIEM export adapter compatibility and sample ingestion envelopes
body:
Purpose:
This working reference defines a cross‑platform export adapter model (the "ingestion envelope") and compatibility guidance for Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs, and Azure Sentinel (EventHub/Log Analytics). It also codifies RBAC v2 guardrails, audit schema fields required for evidence automation, and a customer requirements checklist for onboarding new SIEM integrations.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: security engineers, integration SREs, solutions engineers, and third‑party integrator teams.
- Scope: payload shape, minimal required fields, optional enrichment, redaction presets, delivery semantics (batching/retries/idempotency), and test vectors for partner compatibility checks.
- Out of scope: downstream SIEM parsing rules maintained by the customer; this doc focuses on the outbound adapter and contract surface.

Design principles (high level):
- Single canonical audit schema: every exported event must map to a canonical set of audit fields. Consumers may add tags/metadata but must preserve the canonical fields.
- Minimum disclosure: exporters apply tenant & PII redaction presets. Customers can opt into expanded fields via an allowlist.
- Evidenceable exports: every batch must include a proof artifact (hash + signature reference) so downstream evidence automation can reconcile delivered vs emitted events.
- Compatibility by adapter: we ship small adapter transforms (HEC, Datadog, Sentinel) that map the canonical envelope into the destination envelope.

Canonical audit envelope (required fields):
- envelope_version: semantic version string (e.g., v1.2)
- tenant_id: tenant namespace id (UUID)
- event_id: globally unique id (UUID)
- created_at: ISO8601 timestamp (UTC)
- actor: freeform (user/service) + actor_type (user|service|system)
- action: short string (e.g., model.generate, key.rotate)
- resource: resource path (e.g., /models/llama-2/instances/abc123)
- outcome: success|failure|partial|skipped
- request_id: correlation id (if available)
- rbactx: minimal RBAC v2 context string (role, scope)
- payload_summary: short summary field used for quick indexing
- pii_masking: value from masking profile applied (none|partial|full)

Optional enrichment fields:
- model_version, latency_ms, token_count, cost_estimate_cents, error_code, parent_event_id, tags (list)

Evidence automation fields (delivery proof):
- batch_id: id for the exported batch
- event_count: numeric count
- proof_hash: SHA256 of canonical events concatenated in canonical order (hex)
- signer_key_id: key fingerprint used to sign the proof_hash (references KMS entry)
- signature: base64 detached signature of proof_hash
- proof_url: optional retrievable proof bundle URL (signed, time‑limited)

Destination adapter mappings (examples):
1) Splunk HEC (recommended fields):
- HEC envelope: {"time": created_at, "host": "redwood-export", "source": "redwood.audit", "sourcetype": "_json"} + event = canonical envelope.
- Important: include X-Redwood-Tenant header with tenant_id, and X-Export-Batch header with batch_id.
- Sample note: HEC indexing rules should map event.action to top level event_action field to allow fast searches.

2) Datadog Logs intake (recommended fields):
- Datadog expected keys: "ddsource": "redwood", "service": "inference", "hostname": "exporter", "message": canonical envelope as JSON.
- Use "ddtags": "tenant:<tenant_id>,env:<env>" for quick facets.
- For high‑cardinality tagging (model_version), prefer tag prefix model:<ver>.

3) Azure Sentinel (Event Hub -> Log Analytics):
- Envelope: EventHub batch of JSON records. Each record = canonical envelope.
- Ensure records include a stable partitioning_key = tenant_id when using Event Hub partitioning to guarantee ordering for tenant retention and evidence correlation.
- Provide a companion ingestion manifest describing schema_version and required fields for Log Analytics transforms.

Batching & throughput guidance:
- Default export QoS tiers: realtime_small (<= 1 rps, batch <= 1 event), standard (<= 50 rps, batch size 50), bulk (>=50 rps, batch size up to 500).
- Batching is boundary‑aligned on batch_id. Each batch should contain <= 10MB payload after adapter transform to stay within common SIEM limits.
- Backpressure: adapters must honor 429/503 with exponential backoff (base 250ms, cap 60s) and jitter.
- Idempotency: use batch_id + attempt_number; consumers MUST accept replays of same batch_id and deduplicate by event_id.

RBAC v2 export guardrails:
- Only users/roles with export:read permission can create export jobs.
- Role-scoped export: exports must include rbactx; adapters must reject attempts to include fields outside allowed scope (customer allowlist).
- Audit trail: every export job create/update/delete action must itself be an audit event in the canonical schema and linked via parent_event_id.

PII and retention controls:
- Default masking profiles: none, partial (email -> masked), full (remove fields flagged as pii).
- Customers must provide a retention period per destination. Adapters attach retention metadata when supported by target (e.g., Datadog tag retention window).

Operational test vectors (minimal set to validate a connector):
- TV1: single event realtime_small with PII masked = none. Verify event lands and searchable by event_id.
- TV2: batch of 250 events including mixed outcomes and model_version tags. Verify batch proof_hash and signature validate and event_count matches.
- TV3: replay same batch_id twice; check downstream dedup by event_id.
- TV4: forced 429 from endpoint; verify exponential backoff and eventual success on retry.

Customer onboarding checklist (what solutions/sales/SEs should collect):
- Destination type (HEC/Datadog/EventHub), endpoint URL, auth method (token/cert), allowed IP ranges (for firewall rules), desired QoS tier, retention policy, data residency constraints, PII allowlist/denylist, sample Log/Index mapping (example Splunk sourcetype mapping), SLA expectations for delivery.

Testing and validation plan:
- Run integration test harness (repo link in linked_artifacts) using the operational test vectors.
- Provide partner a JSON schema (openapi style) for the canonical envelope and adapter transform examples.
- For enterprise customers: perform signed delivery proof verification during onboarding (verify proof_hash/signature against KMS signer_key_id).

Migration and versioning:
- envelope_version is mandatory. Adapters must support two most recent minor versions; deprecation notices follow a minimum 90‑day window.

Open questions / TODOs (working):
- Standardize rbactx shape for cross‑org RBAC view (short term: freeform string; longer term: structured claim set).
- Decide TLS mutual auth baseline for high sensitivity tenants.
- Implement automated replay‑proof retrieval endpoint (proof_url) and retention rules for proof bundles.

Appendix: sample payloads (condensed)
- Splunk HEC example (single event):
  HEC headers: Authorization: Splunk <token>, X-Redwood-Tenant: <tenant_id>, X-Export-Batch: <batch_id>
  Payload: {
    "time": "2025-01-15T12:34:56Z",
    "host": "redwood-export",
    "source": "redwood.audit",
    "event": {
      "envelope_version": "v1.2",
      "tenant_id": "<tenant_id>",
      "event_id": "<uuid>",
      "created_at": "2025-01-15T12:34:55Z",
      "actor": "service:batch-exporter",
      "action": "export.batch.send",
      "resource": "/exports/1234",
      "outcome": "success"
    }
  }

- Datadog example (single event):
  HTTP fields: API key in header, ddsource=redwood, ddtags=tenant:<tenant_id>,env:prod
  Body: {
    "message": "<canonical envelope as JSON>",
    "service": "inference-exports"
  }

- Sentinel EventHub: produce array of canonical envelopes; ensure partition_key=tenant_id set on the EventData record.

Contact and ownership:
- Primary owner: Priya Desai (security-and-compliance). Integration SRE: Evan Park. Solutions lead for partner onboarding: Liam O'Connor.

If approved, next steps: formalize JSON Schema artifact, add adapter unit tests to exporter repo, schedule partner compatibility run with Splunk/Datadog/Sentinel test environments and move doc to final.
